Draw the board

Source: R/plot-map.R
dp_plot_map.Rd

Renders the board as a map. Every province is drawn as a territory rather than a point: seas in blue, coastal land and inland in two shades of buff, with coastlines picked out against the province borders. A supply centre wears its name on a chip coloured for the power that holds it, so the balance of the game is visible at a glance. Units are tokens in their power's colour – a circle for an army, a diamond for a fleet – and units awaiting a retreat are ringed in red.

Usage

dp_plot_map(
  game,
  orders = NULL,
  labels = TRUE,
  ownership = TRUE,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL
)

Arguments

game

A dp_game object.

orders

Optional orders to draw over the board, as a dp_orders tibble. TRUE draws the orders the game last resolved, if it has any.

labels

Draw the three-letter province codes. Default TRUE.

ownership

Colour each supply centre's chip for the power that holds it. Default TRUE; FALSE leaves every chip neutral.

title

Plot title. NULL uses the current turn.

subtitle

Plot subtitle. NULL summarises the position.

Value

A ggplot2 object.

Details

Terrain and ownership are deliberately encoded in different ways. Terrain gets the large quiet fills and ownership the small saturated chips, because washing a power's colour across a whole province makes a blue power's land look like sea.

Pass orders to draw the turn on the board: solid arrows for moves and retreats, dashed for supports, dash-dotted for convoys. If the orders have been adjudicated, and so carry a success column, the arrows that failed are marked with a cross at their head.

The board is schematic. Provinces sit at fixed coordinates and their shapes come from tessellating the plane between them, so the outlines are suggestive of Europe rather than a faithful coastline.

The board is close to square. Give it a close-to-square figure: the default 7 x 5 of many rendering setups leaves a third of the width empty and squeezes the province names together.

See also

Other plot: autoplot.dp_game(), dp_palette(), dp_plot_centres(), dp_plot_sc_history(), dp_plot_supply_heatmap(), dp_plot_winrates()

Examples

dp_plot_map(dp_new_game())


g <- dp_new_game()
dp_plot_map(g, orders = dp_example_orders())
